newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Soccer-McAteer seeks an Irish passport.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-McAteer seeks an Irish passport.

text.p: Liverpool's Jason McAteer made a brief court appearance to try and to secure an Irish passport in time for Sunday's World Cup qualifier against Iceland, Irish media reported on Friday.

McAteer, who has been using a British passport until now, made a declaration of fidelity and loyalty to the Irish State at a two-minute hearing in Ballybay, County Monaghan before Judge Flan Brennan on Thursday.

FAI officials were confident the vital document would be in their possession later today, ending a rush to meet strict FIFA rules which now require all players to produce a national passport before games.
McAteer, who is in line to win his 20th cap on Sunday, is the third member of Mick McCarthy's squad to be granted an Irish passport.
The soccer star qualified to play for the Republic of Ireland through his grandparents, who were born in the northern County of Down.

Another Irish soccer star Niall Quinn, the Republic of Ireland and Sunderland forward, is to undergo surgery next week to repair a torn cruciate ligament in his knee and will miss the rest of the season.

The injury, which Quinn sustained in Sunderland's game against Coventry City on September 21, is identical to that which kept him out for six months of the 1993/4 season and caused him to miss the World Cup in the United States.
